new_libraries.name: Pico_USB_Disp
new_libraries.author: Hideto Kikuchi / PJラボ (@pcjpnet)
new_libraries.sentence: Drive an external monitor from a microcontroller through a USB display adapter, with no PC or OS required.
new_libraries.paragraph: Output Full HD (1920x1080) video from a Raspberry Pi Pico / Pico 2 (USB host on two GPIOs via PIO) or an ESP32-S2/S3/P4. Also runs on Teensy 4.0/4.1 and on PC via libusb. Supported adapters: DisplayLink DL-1x0/1x5 on all platforms; MCT Trigger 6 and MacroSilicon MS912x/MS913x on ESP32-P4 and PC (USB High-Speed required). Resolution is selected automatically from the monitor's EDID. Simple partial-update drawing API, with optional LovyanGFX and LVGL v9 integration.

library.name: Plynx
library.author: Plynx, derived from Blynk library by Volodymyr Shymanskyy
library.sentence: Control your Arduino, ESP32 or ESP8266 from the Plynx app.
library.paragraph: Talks to a Plynx (or Blynk-legacy) server. Default server yes.plynx.cc. It supports  WiFi, BLE, Bluetooth, Ethernet, GSM, USB, Serial. Works with many boards like ESP8266, ESP32, Arduino UNO, Nano, Due, Mega, Zero, MKR100, Yun, Raspberry Pi, Particle, Energia, ARM mbed, Intel Edison/Galileo/Joule, BBC micro:bit, DFRobot, RedBearLab, Microduino, LinkIt ONE ...

library.name: ProsecCoAP
library.author: Pasquale Lafiosca
library.sentence: CoAP client/server library for Arduino-compatible hardware.
library.paragraph: ProsecCoAP 🥂 is a lightweight implementation of a Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) node, that includes client/server, request/response and the asynchronous observe pattern, enabling robust M2M communication for IoT projects.
